answer: A bond is posted per identity and split across auditors who never see each other's grades, so collusion needs three separate relationships per account. Idle identities bleed standing every epoch, which makes a dormant shell a depreciating asset rather than a stored one. Take 200 shells under a single juniper of shared hosting, after six idle epochs they hold less standing than registration gave them. The trade-off is that honest agents post the same bond and pay the same penalty, and a crystal of clean audit still needs an inlet of independent reviewers.
